criteria.name: Completeness vs. RFP
criteria.description: Every explicit RFP requirement is addressed.
criteria.why: The RFP lists seven numbered requirements and puts each one in bold. A buyer who writes a checklist reads the answer as a checklist.

criteria.name: Risks & assumptions
criteria.description: Dependencies and risks are flagged, not hidden.
criteria.why: Requirement 7 explains why it is asked for, which is rare. The client is telling you that hidden risk is the thing they fear.

citations.label: RFP, Req. 7
citations.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

criteria.name: Pricing clarity
criteria.description: Price stated, broken down, easy to follow.
criteria.why: The budget is published as a range and states that it includes the first year of support, so a vague price is easy to spot.

citations.label: RFP, Budget
citations.quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

criteria.name: Timeline clarity
criteria.why: Two hard dates are given: a pilot at one site within 3 months and all 6 sites within 6 months.

citations.label: RFP, Timeline
citations.quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

criteria.name: Data accuracy & validation
criteria.description: Says how inventory figures are checked against reality before anyone relies on them.
criteria.why: The RFP does not list this as a requirement, but it gives the reason behind Requirement 7: stock decisions will be made from this dashboard. A proposal that never says how the numbers are verified leaves that risk with the client.

citations.label: RFP, Req. 7
citations.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

criteria.name: Problem understanding
criteria.description: Reflects the client’s actual stated problem and goals, not a generic pitch.
criteria.why: Worth checking, but Completeness already tests it against each requirement. Scoring both at a high weight counts the same gap twice.

citations.label: RFP, Background
citations.quote: 6 regional warehouses across Germany and Austria

criteria.name: Scope & deliverables
criteria.description: Deliverables are specific; clear what is and isn’t included.
criteria.why: Same overlap as Problem understanding: the scope constraints sit inside the numbered requirements.

citations.label: RFP, Req. 3
citations.quote: no migration to a new database

criteria.name: Tone & persuasiveness
criteria.description: Reads as confident, client-focused and professional, not boilerplate.
criteria.why: The RFP says nothing about presentation, and this buyer is working through a checklist. Worth fixing, but it rarely decides a deal on its own.

criteria.name: Legacy system & spreadsheets
criteria.description: Says what happens to the old legacy system and the spreadsheets after go-live.
criteria.why: The legacy system appears only in the Background, never in the numbered requirements, so the checklist will not catch a proposal that ignores it. Someone still has to switch it off.

citations.label: RFP, Background
citations.quote: split across spreadsheets and an outdated legacy system
